The single AxClass ConDemoErDataProvider was produced entirely through prepare(create) -> search / get_object_info / get_method / find_references -> validate_code(references+syntax) -> d365fo_file(action=create); no hand-authored XML, and the ER model, mapping and format were correctly left out of the AOT per the case scope limit. Three non-blocking defects observed. (1) KNOWLEDGE_GAP (primary): get_knowledge(topic=electronic-reporting) states two rules that are false against this AOT - [a] "To extend ER model mapping: implement IERModelMappingExtension on your class": search finds NO symbol IERModelMappingExtension or ERModelMappingExtension anywhere in the index; [b] "For custom data sources: create a class implementing ERIDataSourceProvider and register it": ERIDataSourceProvider is an ER DESIGNER interface with the single member "public ERIDataSource getDataSource()", find_references returns exactly ONE consumer in the whole AOT (ERLookupRootComponentUIBuilder.getDataSource), and its return type ERIDataSource is not an X++ type at all, so an application data-source class implementing it would not compile. The correct grounded answer, which the KB never states, is that an ER application data source is a PLAIN public X++ class: ER binds it in the model-mapping designer via the data-source type "Dynamics 365 for Operations \ Class", handled framework-side by ERClassDataSourceHandler / ERClassDataSourceHandlerExtension (ElectronicReporting model). There is no registration API to call. Following the KB literally produces a non-compiling class. (2) VALIDATOR_GAP: validate_code(mode="references") reported "all 18 reference(s) verified ... Safe to proceed" for a class body that xppc then rejected TWICE - first "The name TaxAmountCur does not denote a class, a table, or an extended data type" (5 errors), then "A reference to Dynamics.AX.FiscalBooks ... is required to compile this module" on a plain select from CustInvoiceJour. Both symbols EXIST in the index (TaxAmountCur -> model Tax; CustInvoiceJour -> model Foundation) but are NOT VISIBLE from the target model: the resolver checks existence only and ignores the sandbox Descriptor ModuleReferences. This is the 7th consecutive false result from that tool and the expensive kind - it green-lights a write that costs a full build cycle. The second variant is subtler: CustInvoiceJour lives in an ALREADY-REFERENCED package (ApplicationSuite/Foundation), yet ANY select on it demands the FiscalBooks package because FiscalBooks contributes a table extension; isolated with a 6-line throwaway probe class (select firstonly RecId, InvoiceId from CustInvoiceJour -> same FiscalBooks error). (3) Minor build-diagnostics defect: xppc method locations come back with a stray backtick prefix in the element path (dynamics://Class/ConDemoErDataProvider/Method/[backtick]getInvoiceTotals) and the reported line/col pair was identical, (43,5)-(43,38), for two DIFFERENT statements across successive builds, which cost one wasted edit cycle before the probe isolated the real trigger. Design decision recorded for the golden: the provider reads FMRental / FMRentalCharge (FleetManagement, already in ModuleReferences) instead of CustInvoiceJour, so NO package reference had to be added - Contoso/Descriptor/Contoso.xml ModuleReferences is left exactly as found (ApplicationFoundation, ApplicationPlatform, ApplicationSuite, FleetManagement, Directory, Ledger, ContactPerson, Currency, Dimensions, PersonnelCore, GeneralLedger, SourceDocumentationTypes). A CustInvoiceJour-based golden would have required FiscalBooks + Tax and would not reproduce on a clean sandbox.
